title: A multivalent RNA affinity tag enables selective purification of tagged RNAs and bound proteins.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran scripts/paper_context.py (abstract plus whole open-access full text, 113,663 characters): zero accessions in text, zero text-mined accessions, no GEO/SRA/BioProject/dbGaP links, empty Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI. Data availability statement reads only 'available in the article and in its online supplementary data'. Searched the full text for GEO, GSE, SRA, BioProject, Zenodo, figshare, Dryad, 'source data' - no hits. Tried to pull the single supplementary item (gkag735_Supplemental_File) three ways: Europe PMC supplementaryFiles HEAD returned HTTP 500, the full GET and the Europe PMC fulltextRepo URL both failed with DNS errors. So no data file was opened.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That Supplementary Table S1 lists promoter, tag position and nucleotide sequence for each construct and Supplementary Table S2 lists the FLAG-MCP (FLAG-tagged MS2 coat protein) nucleotide and amino-acid sequence; that the quantitative results are percent-of-input recoveries read off gels and RT-qPCR (reverse-transcription quantitative PCR) in Figures 1-5 and Supplementary Figures S1-S10; the specific numbers quoted (3% to 50% recovery for D8-IRES, 13.3% to 60% for FS1-IRES, 58.4 +/- 4.4% recovery of a 1.6 kb reporter, 14.0 +/- 0.4% recovery and ~79,000-fold enrichment for FS4). None of these were seen in a file.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset is deposited anywhere: no accession, no repository, no Zenodo/Dryad record. The only attachment is one supplementary document, and my three download attempts failed (Europe PMC HTTP 500, then DNS errors), so even that was not inspected.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table of measurements. Every quantitative value (percent RNA bound or eluted) lives inside a bar chart or gel panel in a figure, so any label would have to be digitised from images or re-typed from figure text.

a3_inputs_present.note: Paper text says construct nucleotide sequences are in Supplementary Table S1, so inputs would be sequences rather than accessions - but this is from the paper text only, and it is roughly 10-25 constructs.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated clearly in the text: pmol of RNA loaded, percent of input recovered, mM magnesium and EDTA, degrees Celsius, minutes of incubation.

a5_enough_rows.note: Order of tens of measurements, not thousands: a handful of tag designs (D8, FS1, FS2, FS4) crossed with a handful of host RNAs (Nluc, Gluc, mCherry, IRES, MYC, MS2, DRACH, EGFP reporter) and small titration series (5 magnesium levels, ~6 time points), each in triplicate. Far below the ~1,500-row bar; no count verified in any file.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Whatever data exists is a few kilobytes of numbers and sequences; laptop feasibility is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable - there is no download to compare against the paper, because the supplementary file could not be retrieved and nothing is deposited in a repository.

a8_label_provenance.note: The measurements are genuine physical readouts (gel band quantification, RT-qPCR, Western blot), not another model's predictions and not computed from the features.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (an RNA language model) would be the natural backbone for RNA-sequence-to-function tasks
backbone.licence: open (not verified for this evaluation, since the project died at Part A)

integration.join_key: none - the paper carries no standard identifier (no UniProt, Ensembl, PDB or accession) for its constructs
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: with roughly a dozen engineered constructs and no shared identifiers there is nothing to join to a large resource.

controls.positive_control: Would have been the known requirement of magnesium for D8 aptamer folding, which any working model should recover.
controls.negative_control: Untagged IRES RNA, which the authors show gives no detectable elution signal.
controls.external_validation: None available - no second dataset measures Sephadex/dextran binding of these tag designs.

honest_claim_h3: At best a model could claim: among about a dozen hand-designed dextran-binding RNA tag constructs from one laboratory, purification recovery tracks aptamer copy number and magnesium level - a claim the paper's own figures already make more directly than any model could.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the sequence and structure of an RNA affinity tag to predict how much tagged RNA a bead column recovers.
plain_idea.train_on: What a model would see: the nucleotide sequence of each tag-plus-cargo RNA construct, the number of aptamer copies, and the buffer conditions (magnesium, salt, detergent, temperature, time). Verified count: unknown; the paper implies only tens of distinct condition-construct combinations, all read off figures.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be percent of input RNA recovered in the elution fraction, measured by staining and quantifying RNA bands on a gel or by reverse-transcription quantitative PCR in the authors' own hands.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If it worked, groups engineering RNA purification tags (the Jaffrey laboratory and synthetic-biology labs using F30-scaffold aptamers) could rank new tag designs before cloning them. But with only tens of measurements from one laboratory, nothing generalisable could be learned.

ml_idea: The only task this paper supports is predicting bead-binding recovery of an engineered RNA tag from its sequence and buffer conditions. There are tens of such measurements, they exist only as bars in figures, and the paper's own optimisation experiments already answer the question directly, so there is no machine-learning project here. Note for the record: searches surfaced listings for aptamer-affinity prediction models (DeepAptamer, AIoptamer) trained on large SELEX libraries, but I did not retrieve those papers and they are irrelevant once Part A fails.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, nothing timed: a few dozen short RNA sequences would embed in seconds on a CPU. Compute was never the constraint; the absence of data is.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the quantitative measurements the paper actually reports. Skimming the figure callouts in the full text takes ten minutes and shows the answer is tens, not thousands - that alone kills it.

verdict_reason: Wet-lab methods paper with no deposited dataset: no accession, no repository record, and quantitative values exist only inside figure panels. Fails A1 (nothing downloadable; the single supplementary document would not retrieve), A2 (no label column - it would have to be digitised from bar charts) and decisively A5 (tens of measurements from one laboratory, against a ~1,500-row bar).
